hints.title: Minimal Subarray Sum Contraction Obstacle
hints.text: Checking all possible contiguous slices requires quadratic time. Because all values in the array are positive, expanding the right boundary increases the running sum while shrinking the left boundary decreases it. How can you track the shortest valid slice in a single pass?

hints.title: Dynamic Window Shrinking Invariant
hints.text: Expand the right edge of the slice until the accumulated total meets or exceeds the target. Once valid, shrink from the left to find the minimal length that still satisfies the threshold.

hints.title: Sliding Window Contraction Procedure
hints.text: Initialize min_len to infinity, left to zero, and current_sum to zero. Loop right through the array, adding nums[right] to current_sum. While current_sum is greater than or equal to target, record the candidate length right minus left plus one, subtract nums[left] from current_sum, and increment left. Return zero if min_len was never updated, else return min_len.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def minSubArrayLen(self, target: int, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        min_len = float('inf')
        left = 0
        current_sum = 0
        for right in range(len(nums)):
            current_sum += nums[right]
            while current_sum >= target:
                min_len = min(min_len, right - left + 1)
                current_sum -= nums[left]
                left += 1
        return 0 if min_len == float('inf') else min_len
```

variables: N: length of nums array (1 <= N <= 10^5)
complexity.notes: Dynamic sliding window with amortized O(N) time and O(1) space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating every subarray sum takes O(N^2) time, which times out when N=10^5 (10^10 operations).
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Since each element enters and leaves the window at most once, the dynamic window runs in 2N steps with O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Returning 0 when no valid subarray exists and understanding the strict positivity precondition that makes monotonic window expansion work.
